correctness.rationale: Exact model and one-step conditional probabilities are specified. Survival at root degree one is the explicit central binomial p_n. Root/leaf mean recurrences and the mixed-moment identity c_{n+1}=c_n+d_{n+1}-p_n/[2(n-1)] are derived from conditional Bernoulli events, not fitted numerically. Their closed forms satisfy base cases, produce the stated covariance, and a strictly decreasing ratio q_{n+1}/q_n proves the sign for all integers n>=4. Independent variance recurrences and Stirling give the sharp covariance and correlation scales. A standalone Python program exhausts 6,917 degree vectors and checks 2,993 further rational recurrences; finite tests are not treated as infinite proofs.

originality.rationale: Closest published and archival sources were compared on observable, process model, and logical implication, including a superficially identical root-degree/global-leaf claim for uniform recursive trees that cannot imply the BA result. An early PORT article was inspected and found to use a distinct root attachment weight. Fixed-dimensional aged-degree theorems and global degree-class covariances do not cover the mixed tagged-root versus extensive leaf-count moment. Historical priority remains a disclosed unresolved risk without decisive contradiction.
residual_risks: An unindexed historical article on tagged-vertex/global-count joint moments could precede this formula; this search does not prove absolute historical priority.
The article on preferential attachment leaf statistics from 2026 postdates the archive-source cutoff and is considered for overlap only, not as the archival primary source.
No independent expert audit has been conducted.

value.rationale: The dependence of one distinguished early hub on the extensive leaf population is a natural, independently meaningful structural observable of degree-proportional growth. The exact positive all-size sign, square-root increasing covariance, and inverse-square-root decaying correlation provide a non-marginal local/global law and a stark comparison with uniform recursive trees whose analogous covariance stays bounded. No arbitrary parameter slice or table recomputation is needed.
